rows.name: Linux MD RAID5 with scheduled check/repair and a file-serving layer
rows.reason: Linux RAID5 documents consistency/check/repair, not end-to-end checksum repair or a Windows-native replacement. Scheduling/corruption guarantees unverified; seven-disk configuration, scheduler and ESXi disk presentation untested.

rows.name: StableBit DrivePool with Scanner integration — pooling component reference
rows.reason: Windows pooling/evacuation component, not verified parity/scrub protection. FAQ documents duplication; parity/checksum scrubbing unverified. Separate verified protection needed; Windows Server 2019 and historical-version compatibility unverified.

rows.name: FreeNAS 11.3 with OpenZFS RAIDZ
rows.reason: RAIDZ, checksum-directed repair and scheduled scrubs address seven-disk integrity. Pool creation requires migration; versioned guide discourages production virtualization. Validate disk visibility, memory allocation and failure recovery.

rows.name: Unraid
rows.reason: Scheduled parity checks and failed-disk reconstruction fit a media-storage alternative, although parity correction alone cannot identify and heal silently corrupted file data.

rows.name: OpenZFS
rows.reason: Checksum-verified RAIDZ, scheduled scrubs and redundancy-based repair directly address the requirement; deployment needs an appropriate storage OS and reliable access to individual disks.

rows.name: Linux MD software RAID
rows.reason: Linux RAID5/6 offers array checks, repair, recovery and mismatch counters. Scheduling/file serving require separate integration; redundancy consistency does not equal end-to-end file-checksum validation.

rows.name: Unraid
rows.reason: Unraid supports scheduled parity checks; correcting parity from data does not establish integrity repair. Retain for verification: pool/filesystem choices, seven-disk layout and 2020 availability remain unresolved.

rows.name: FreeNAS 11.3 with a seven-disk ZFS RAIDZ1 pool
rows.reason: FreeNAS 11.3 seven-disk RAIDZ1 supports integrity checks/correction if separate OS/single parity are acceptable. RAID5 equivalence/integration unverified; production virtualization discouraged. Pool creation requires moving existing data elsewhere.

rows.name: OpenZFS
rows.reason: 2012 manual documents RAIDZ1/checksum scrub repair. Retain storage engine; host/scheduler selection, RAIDZ1 acceptance and seven-disk ESXi/Windows integration remain unverified.

rows.name: SnapRAID
rows.reason: Windows-compatible parity/checksum recovery for mostly static Plex files. Protection stops at latest sync; scrub detects, fix repairs. Neither continuous RAID5 nor a complete pooling layer.

rows.name: StableBit DrivePool with optional StableBit Scanner integration
rows.reason: DrivePool duplicates ordinary files; optional Scanner can evacuate damaged drives. Full copies replace parity; consistency checks do not establish silent-corruption checksum repair. Server 2019 compatibility needs checking.

rows.name: Unraid parity array
rows.reason: Array UI supports scheduled parity checks/disk reconstruction. Correcting checks align parity with data; they do not establish silently corrupted file correctness. ESXi integration unverified.

rows.name: OpenShot Video Editor
rows.reason: Its timeline editing, video effects and animation tools do not provide disk pooling, RAID parity, storage scrubbing or array recovery.

rows.name: OpenShot Video Editor
rows.reason: Video timeline, effects and animation editing does not replace storage pooling or array maintenance. Shared media/Plex association establishes no usable transfer.
